summary: For the four semibrace identities printed in Dietzel's Problem 3, OWR9/2023, every nonempty meet-semilattice with any prescribed distinguished element admits a semibrace via right projection. A realization that is also an L-algebra exists exactly when the distinguished element is greatest; in every such realization the logical order equals the original meet order. Under the separately attested meet-monoid convention, both existence questions require a greatest element. The result concerns existence, not classification of all multiplications, self-similarity or additional cancellation axioms. It includes arbitrary infinite and nondistributive semilattices.
priority_statement: This note is attributed exposition and explicit verification of the full printed existence answer. The joint multiplication, greatest element when the first argument is below the second and their meet otherwise, is exactly Castiglioni-San Martin's 2016 operation (arXiv:1611.09589v1, p.7, Example3.5(4)); their bounded semilattice means greatest element only, with no bottom assumption. Its final article is l-Hemi-Implicative Semilattices, Studia Logica106(2018),675-690, DOI10.1007/s11225-017-9759-3, online3October2017. The inspected preprint body and final metadata are distinguished. Rump's L-algebra and closure framework and Dietzel's problem are credited. The monoid convention is body-verified already in Dietzel-Menchon-Vendramin arXiv:2206.04955v1,10June2022, before the workshop. No new solution, operation, mechanism, first combined theorem, independent discovery or current worldwide openness is claimed. Historical priority for an earlier explicit combined conclusion remains unestablished; unavailable original2008 bodies and other bounded source gaps are disclosed.
